about: Reviewed findings against data/cshapes.js (CShapes 2.0). CShapes codes de jure changes on the day a treaty was SIGNED, leaves out territorial changes under 10,000 km² and carries present-day borders back where it codes no change (CShapes 2.0 Documentation, G. Schvitz, 2018-12-21, §3). Each finding is judged against the treaty or instrument that made the change, and IntMap draws who governed the ground on that day. Read by scripts/build-cshapes.mjs: `--review` applies `edges` (a change moved to the day it took effect) and `ground` (whole island polygons moved from one record to another for a span; a polygon is moved only when every vertex of its outer ring lies inside `within`, and a polygon partly inside fails the build — `ground` cuts nothing) and `cuts` (a PART of an outline moved to another record for a span, cut along a line from `regions` — each derived from a cited record and photographed in scripts/cshapes/regions.json by `--regions`; scripts/cshapes/cuts.mjs) to the committed bundle, and copies `notes` into it as `review.notes`, which js/time-borders.js shows on the card of the outline they name. `units` declares an outline CShapes does not have (its code is IntMap's, not a Gleditsch-Ward code). `examined` are findings looked at and NOT changed, with the reason. Gate: npm run check:cshapes (re-applying this file to the committed bundle must change nothing, and every entry is measured on the bundle).

7401.name: Ryukyu Islands
7401.basis: IntMap's own code for the Nansei Islands under United States administration (1946-01-29 to 1972-05-14). CShapes 2.0 has no such unit and assigns no code; 7401 is chosen beside Japan's 740 because Japan kept residual sovereignty. It is not a Gleditsch-Ward code.

3681.name: Memel Territory
3681.basis: IntMap's own code for the Klaipėda (Memel) Territory under the High Commissioner of the Principal Allied Powers (1920-02-15 to 1923-02-18). CShapes 2.0 has no such unit; 3681 is chosen beside Lithuania's 368, to which the Conference of Ambassadors transferred it in 1923. It is not a Gleditsch-Ward code.

ground.withinIs: The Kuril group north-east of the Friza (Vries) Strait up to the strait between Cape Lopatka and Shumshu, which Article 2 of the 1875 treaty makes the boundary. Kamchatka (its southern tip at 156.655 E 50.885 N in this bundle) lies outside.
ground.history: By the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (signed 7 May 1875, in force 22 August 1875) Russia ceded to Japan the eighteen Kuril islands from Shumshu to Urup, the boundary between the two empires being the strait between Cape Lopatka and Shumshu (Art. 2). Japan held them until the Soviet occupation of August-September 1945. CShapes 2.0 draws Shumshu, Atlasov, Paramushir, Onekotan, Kharimkotan, Shiashkotan and Simushir inside Russia for 1886-1945 because its coding rules leave out changes under 10,000 km² and carry present-day borders back where no change is coded (the islands are the same polygons in every Russian row, 1886-2019). The span ends on 14 August 1945, the day CShapes itself ends Japanese rule over Southern Sakhalin, Korea and Taiwan.

sources.cite: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (Treaty for the Exchange of Sakhalin for the Kuril Islands), 7 May 1875, French authentic text, Article 2; Japanese translation 第二款 (太政官布告)
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3 Coding Decisions

ground.withinIs: The Nansei Islands south of 30°N (SCAPIN-677 (b), including Kuchinoshima).
ground.history: SCAPIN-677 of 29 January 1946 separated from Japan, governmentally and administratively, the Ryukyu (Nansei) Islands south of 30°N including Kuchinoshima; the Japanese government's authority there was suspended and the islands were placed under United States military government (the United States Civil Administration of the Ryukyu Islands from December 1950).

sources.cite: SCAPIN-677, Governmental and Administrative Separation of Certain Outlying Areas from Japan, 29 January 1946, §3 (b)

ground.withinIs: The Nansei Islands south of 29°N (Treaty of San Francisco, Art. 3).
ground.history: The Tokara Islands (between 29°N and 30°N) returned to Japanese administration on 10 February 1952 (SCAPIN-677/1 of 5 December 1951). Article 3 of the Treaty of San Francisco (in force 28 April 1952) left the Nansei Shoto south of 29°N under United States administration. CShapes 2.0 has no polygon for the Tokara Islands, so the line this draws does not move on that day; the row edge records the change.

sources.cite: SCAPIN-677/1, 5 December 1951; return of the Tokara Islands, 10 February 1952 (Kagoshima Prefecture, トカラ列島の日本復帰)
Treaty of Peace with Japan (San Francisco), signed 8 September 1951, in force 28 April 1952, Article 3

ground.withinIs: The Ryukyu Islands as USCAR Civil Administration Proclamation No. 27 (25 December 1953) bounds them: 28°N 124°40'E, 24°N 122°E, 24°N 133°E, 27°N 131°50'E, 27°N 128°18'E, 28°N 128°18'E.
ground.history: The Amami Islands returned to Japanese administration on 25 December 1953. USCAR Proclamation No. 27 of the same day fixed the geographical boundaries of the Ryukyu Islands as the area inside 28°N 124°40'E - 24°N 122°E - 24°N 133°E - 27°N 131°50'E - 27°N 128°18'E - 28°N 128°18'E (which keeps Iheya inside and Yoron outside). Administration of the Ryukyu and Daito Islands returned to Japan on 15 May 1972 under the Okinawa Reversion Agreement.

sources.cite: USCAR Civil Administration Proclamation No. 27, Geographical Boundaries of the Ryukyu Islands, 25 December 1953 (as quoted in the 琉球政府章典)
Agreement between Japan and the United States of America concerning the Ryukyu Islands and the Daito Islands, signed 17 June 1971, in force 15 May 1972

edges.history: The Treaty of Annexation was signed at Seoul on 22 August 1910 and, by its Article 8, took effect on the day of its promulgation; it was promulgated on 29 August 1910 (官報号外, 条約第4号). The Korean Empire's government ruled until then. CShapes codes the signing day for every change (codebook §3: 'we code the day on which for example a treaty was signed as the day a territorial change occurred') and starts colonial Korea on 23 August. The two CShapes rows have the same outline, so only the name changes day.

sources.cite: 韓国併合ニ関スル条約, signed 22 August 1910, Article 8; promulgated 29 August 1910, 官報号外 条約第4号
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

edges.history: By the Treaty of Shimonoseki (signed 17 April 1895, ratifications exchanged at Chefoo on 8 May 1895) the Qing ceded Taiwan and the Pescadores to Japan (Art. 2). Nothing changed hands on the signing day: the Qing governor still administered the island, and its officials proclaimed the Republic of Formosa on 25 May 1895. Taiwan was handed over to Japan on 2 June 1895, when Li Jingfang and Governor-General Kabayama Sukenori signed the instrument of transfer off Keelung; Japanese troops had landed at Aodi on 29 May and took Taipei on 7 June. CShapes codes the signing day (codebook §3) and starts the Japanese colony on 17 April. Following the line of southern-sakhalin-1905 (the signing day stands where the new power already governed), the change is drawn on the day Japan received the island.

sources.cite: Treaty of Shimonoseki (馬關條約 / 下関条約), signed 17 April 1895, Article 2; ratifications exchanged at Chefoo 8 May 1895
Instrument of transfer of Taiwan (臺灣受渡ニ関スル公文), signed off Keelung by Li Jingfang and Kabayama Sukenori, 2 June 1895
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

Nothing changed hands on the signing day: the Qing governor still administered the island, and its officials proclaimed the Republic of Formosa on 25 May 1895. Taiwan was handed over to Japan on 2 June 1895, when Li Jingfang and Governor-General Kabayama Sukenori signed the instrument of transfer off Keelung; Japanese troops had landed at Aodi on 29 May and took Taipei on 7 June. CShapes codes the signing day (codebook §3) and starts the Japanese colony on 17 April. Following the line of southern-sakhalin-1905 (the signing day stands where the new power already governed), the change is drawn on the day Japan received the island.

sources.cite: Instrument of transfer of Taiwan (臺灣受渡ニ関スル公文), signed off Keelung by Li Jingfang and Kabayama Sukenori, 2 June 1895
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

edges.history: The Newlands Resolution annexing Hawaii passed the Senate on 6 July 1898 and was signed by President McKinley on 7 July; sovereignty was transferred at ʻIolani Palace on 12 August 1898, the day Wikidata gives as its effective date (P7588). Until then the Republic of Hawaii governed the islands. CShapes starts the United States territory on 6 July.

sources.cite: Joint Resolution to provide for annexing the Hawaiian Islands to the United States (Newlands Resolution), 30 Stat. 750, approved 7 July 1898
Transfer of sovereignty, ʻIolani Palace, Honolulu, 12 August 1898
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

edges.history: The Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed on 6 December 1921; the Dáil approved it on 7 January 1922, and the Irish Free State came into being on 6 December 1922, when its constitution took effect — the day Wikidata gives as the treaty's effective date (P7588). Throughout 1922 Southern Ireland remained part of the United Kingdom, administered from 16 January by the Provisional Government constituted under the treaty and the Irish Free State (Agreement) Act 1922. CShapes starts the separate state on the signing day.

sources.cite: Articles of Agreement for a Treaty between Great Britain and Ireland, signed 6 December 1921
Irish Free State Constitution Act 1922 (13 Geo. 5 c. 1); Constitution of the Irish Free State, in force 6 December 1922
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

edges.history: The Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed on 6 December 1921; the Dáil approved it on 7 January 1922, and the Irish Free State came into being on 6 December 1922, when its constitution took effect — the day Wikidata gives as the treaty's effective date (P7588). Throughout 1922 Southern Ireland remained part of the United Kingdom, administered from 16 January by the Provisional Government constituted under the treaty and the Irish Free State (Agreement) Act 1922. CShapes starts the separate state on the signing day.

sources.cite: Constitution of the Irish Free State (Saorstát Éireann) Act 1922, in force 6 December 1922
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

edges.history: CShapes 2.0 ends the Free City of Danzig on 31 August 1938 and draws its ground by no record from 1 to 29 September 1938, then inside Germany from 30 September 1938 (the row of the Munich Agreement). The Free City existed until 1 September 1939: that day Gauleiter Albert Forster's Staatsgrundgesetz declared it part of the German Reich, and the Reichstag's Gesetz über die Wiedervereinigung der Freien Stadt Danzig mit dem Deutschen Reich of the same day carried the annexation out. The upstream day is a year early; the Free City is drawn until 31 August 1939, and the cut danzig-1938-1939 takes its outline back out of Germany's row for those months.

sources.cite: Staatsgrundgesetz der Freien Stadt Danzig über die Wiedervereinigung mit dem Deutschen Reich, 1 September 1939; Gesetz über die Wiedervereinigung der Freien Stadt Danzig mit dem Deutschen Reich, 1 September 1939
Treaty of Versailles, 28 June 1919, Articles 100-108 (the Free City of Danzig)
Freie Stadt Danzig (German Wikipedia), read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: Germany's CShapes row of 30 September 1938 to 7 May 1945 draws the Free City of Danzig inside the Reich from its first day, eleven months before the annexation of 1 September 1939 (see danzig-annexation-1939). Until then the Free City's own outline is the Free City's.

sources.cite: Staatsgrundgesetz der Freien Stadt Danzig über die Wiedervereinigung mit dem Deutschen Reich, 1 September 1939

cuts.history: Bukovina was a crown land of the Austrian half of the monarchy (Cisleithania) and never part of the Kingdom of Hungary, yet CShapes 2.0 draws it inside Hungary from 3 November 1918 to 9 September 1919 and adds it to Romania on 10 September 1919, the day Austria signed the Treaty of Saint-Germain, whose Article 59 renounces the former Duchy of Bukovina in favour of Romania. From 3 to 10 November 1918 Ukrainian and Romanian national councils divided Czernowitz and the land between them, and no record draws either; Bukovina is drawn in Austria on those days — the state CShapes gives the rest of Cisleithania then, and the one that renounced Bukovina by treaty.

sources.cite: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 10 September 1919, Article 59
Union of Bukovina with Romania (English Wikipedia), timeline of November 1918, read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: The Romanian army entered Czernowitz on 11 November 1918, after the Ukrainian National Committee withdrew on 10 November; the Romanian National Council formed a government of Bukovina on 12 November and the General Congress of Bukovina voted for union with Romania on 28 November 1918. Romania governed Bukovina from then on; Austria renounced it by the Treaty of Saint-Germain (Art. 59), which is the day CShapes 2.0 moves it — from Hungary, which never held it.

sources.cite: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 10 September 1919, Article 59
Union of Bukovina with Romania (English Wikipedia), timeline of November 1918, read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: Article IX of the Treaty of Portsmouth (5 September 1905) ceded Sakhalin south of the fiftieth degree of north latitude to Japan, and the boundary was demarcated on that parallel. CShapes 2.0 ends Southern Sakhalin (7351) at 49.897°N, about 11 km south of the parallel, and draws the strip between in Russia: measured on the bundle, 1,575 km² of the 33,544 km² of Sakhalin south of 50°N, so the outline was 4.7% smaller than the ground the treaty describes.

sources.cite: Treaty of Portsmouth, 5 September 1905, Article IX

cuts.history: The Memel (Klaipėda) Territory — the Prussian land north of the Neman — was Prussian from the Treaty of Melno (1422) and part of the German Empire from 1871. Article 99 of the Treaty of Versailles (signed 28 June 1919, in force 10 January 1920) detached it and placed it at the disposal of the Principal Allied and Associated Powers; the German troops left and a French administration took over on 15 February 1920. CShapes 2.0 carries Lithuania's present border back over it, drawing it in Russia until 15 February 1918 and in Lithuania after, because it leaves out changes under 10,000 km².

sources.cite: Treaty of Versailles, 28 June 1919, Article 99
Klaipėda Region (English Wikipedia): the French temporary military administration from 15 February 1920, read 2026-10-13
G. Schvitz, Cshapes 2.0: Documentation, 21 December 2018, §3

cuts.history: From 15 February 1920 the territory was governed by a High Commissioner of the Principal Allied Powers (the French General Dominique Odry, then Gabriel Petisné from 1 May 1921). After the Klaipėda Revolt of January 1923 the Conference of Ambassadors transferred it to Lithuania on 16 February 1923, and the High Commissioner handed over to Lithuania's plenipotentiary on 19 February 1923. Lithuania did not govern it before then, so it is drawn as its own unit, not inside Lithuania.

sources.cite: Klaipėda Region (English Wikipedia): High Commissioners, 15 February 1920 - 19 February 1923, read 2026-10-13
Decision of the Conference of Ambassadors, 16 February 1923; Convention concerning the Territory of Memel, Paris, 8 May 1924

cuts.history: Lithuania ceded the territory to Germany by the treaty Juozas Urbšys and Joachim von Ribbentrop signed in Berlin in the early hours of 23 March 1939, and German troops entered Memel that day. Germany held the city until the Red Army took it on 28 January 1945. CShapes 2.0 draws the territory in Lithuania until 1 June 1940 and in the Soviet Union after.

sources.cite: Treaty between Germany and Lithuania on the reunion of the Memel Territory with the German Reich, Berlin, 22-23 March 1939
Klaipėda Region (English Wikipedia): the 1939 treaty and the Battle of Memel to 28 January 1945, read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: The Hlučín Region was Prussian from the Treaty of Breslau (11 June 1742) — part of the province of Silesia and of the German Empire — until Article 83 of the Treaty of Versailles gave it to Czechoslovakia; it was handed over on 4 February 1920. CShapes 2.0 draws it inside Austria-Hungary and then Czechoslovakia from 1886 because it carries the Czech border back over a change under 10,000 km² (316.9 km²). CShapes draws no record in the Czech lands from 3 to 10 November 1918; the region was German on those days and is drawn so.

sources.cite: Treaty of Breslau, 11 June 1742; Treaty of Versailles, 28 June 1919, Article 83
Hlučín Region (English Wikipedia), read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: The Treaty of Rapallo (signed 12 November 1920, in force 2 February 1921) fixed the border of Italy and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes: Italy received Gorizia, Trieste and Istria with the west of Carniola (Art. 1), the city of Zara (Art. 2) and the islands of Cres, Lošinj, Lastovo and Palagruža (Art. 3); Fiume became a free state. Italian troops had held this ground since the armistice of November 1918. CShapes 2.0 carries Yugoslavia's post-1947 border back over all of it from 10 September 1919.

sources.cite: Treaty of Rapallo between the Kingdom of Italy and the Kingdom of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, 12 November 1920, Articles 1-4
Treaty of Rapallo (1920) (English Wikipedia), read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: Under the Treaty of Rome (27 January 1924) Fiume was annexed to Italy on 22 February 1924; the Rapallo border otherwise stood until the Axis invasion of Yugoslavia in April 1941. Italy governed this ground until the armistice of 8 September 1943, after which Germany occupied it (the Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral). CShapes 2.0 draws all of it in Yugoslavia.

sources.cite: Treaty of Rome between Italy and the Kingdom of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, 27 January 1924
Armistice of Cassibile, signed 3 September 1943, announced 8 September 1943

cuts.history: The First Vienna Award (2 November 1938) gave Hungary southern Slovakia and the south-west of Subcarpathian Ruthenia, with Uzhhorod (Ungvár), Mukachevo (Munkács) and Berehove (Beregszász). CShapes 2.0 draws the Slovak part in Hungary from 2 November 1938 and leaves the Ruthenian part in Czechoslovakia. The Red Army's East Carpathian offensive took the region in October 1944, most of it secured by 28 October 1944; from then CShapes' own rows draw it (Czechoslovakia, whose government delegation came to Khust that October, then the Soviet Union from 8 May 1945).

sources.cite: First Vienna Award, 2 November 1938
Carpathian Ruthenia (English Wikipedia): the Vienna Award and the Soviet takeover, read 2026-10-13

cuts.history: Carpatho-Ukraine proclaimed its independence on 15 March 1939 as the Hungarian army invaded it; Hungary formally annexed the territory on 16 March and the last organised resistance ended on 18 March 1939. Hungary governed it until the Soviet offensive of October 1944. CShapes 2.0 draws no change there: it keeps Czechoslovakia whole apart from the Munich and Vienna cessions until 1945.

sources.cite: Carpatho-Ukraine (English Wikipedia): the invasion of 14-18 March 1939 and the annexation of 16 March, read 2026-10-13
Carpathian Ruthenia (English Wikipedia): the Soviet takeover, 28 October 1944, read 2026-10-13

danzig-free-city.is: The Free City of Danzig as CShapes 2.0 itself draws it (code 291, 1919-06-28 to 1938-08-31): the line is the bundle's own, so cutting along it adds no new line.

bukovina-1919.is: The ground CShapes 2.0 adds to Romania on 10 September 1919, the day Austria signed the Treaty of Saint-Germain renouncing Bukovina (Art. 59): Romania's row of that day less its row of the day before. Both lines are CShapes' own.

karafuto-50n.is: Sakhalin south of the fiftieth parallel, the boundary Article IX of the Treaty of Portsmouth (1905) states. The box's other three edges lie in the Tatar Strait, La Pérouse Strait and the Sea of Okhotsk, so the parallel is the only line it draws on land.

memel-territory.is: The Klaipėda (Memel) Territory as OpenHistoricalMap draws it (relation «Memelland»): north of the Neman and its Skirvytė arm, up to the pre-1919 German-Russian border. It is the same land as OpenHistoricalMap's Lithuania of 1923-1939 less its Lithuania of 1939 (measured: 0.0 km² apart).

hlucin-region.is: The Hlučín Region: what OpenHistoricalMap's Czechoslovakia gains on 4 February 1920 (its relation from that day less its relation of 1918-11-05 to 1920-02-04), the part holding Hlučín. Measured 316.99 km² against the 316.9 km² the region is stated to cover.

julian-march-1920.is: Italy as OpenHistoricalMap draws it from 1920 to 22 February 1924 (before Fiume was annexed), within a box around the northern Adriatic that holds the whole Italian-Yugoslav border of the Treaty of Rapallo and Zara; the box only keeps the photograph small — it holds every place where this Italy meets CShapes' Yugoslavia.

julian-march-1924.is: Italy as OpenHistoricalMap draws it from 1929 to 1940, within the same box: the Rapallo border with Fiume, annexed under the Treaty of Rome (1924). OpenHistoricalMap's Italy of 1924-1929 draws the same eastern border (it differs from this one only by the Vatican City).

ruthenia-vienna-1938.is: The part of Subcarpathian Ruthenia the First Vienna Award (2 November 1938) gave to Hungary — Uzhhorod, Mukachevo, Berehove: OpenHistoricalMap's Hungary of 2 November 1938 to 14 March 1939 within its Subcarpathian Ruthenia of 1920-1938.

carpatho-ukraine-1939.is: The rest of Subcarpathian Ruthenia (Carpatho-Ukraine), occupied by Hungary in March 1939: OpenHistoricalMap's Hungary of 14 March to 4 April 1939 less its Hungary of 2 November 1938.

notes.en: IntMap draws the northern Kuril Islands (Shumshu to Simushir) in Japan until 14 August 1945: Russia ceded the Kurils from Shumshu to Urup to Japan by the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1875). CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, places them in Russia because it carries present-day borders back for changes under 10,000 km².
notes.jp: この輪郭では、北千島（占守島〜新知島）を 1945 年 8 月 14 日まで日本に含めて描いている。1875 年の樺太・千島交換条約で、ロシアは占守島から得撫島までの千島列島を日本に譲った。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は、1 万 km² 未満の領土変更を記録せず今日の国境を遡らせるため、これらの島をロシアに置いている。

notes.en: The Treaty of Annexation, signed on 22 August 1910, took effect only when it was promulgated on 29 August (Art. 8); until then the Korean Empire's government ruled, so it is drawn here although CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, starts the Japanese colony on 23 August.
notes.jp: 8 月 22 日に調印された韓国併合条約は、8 月 29 日の公布で初めて施行された（第 8 条）。それまでは大韓帝国の政府が統治していたため、この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 が日本の植民地を 8 月 23 日から始めているのに対し、ここでは大韓帝国として描いている。

notes.en: Drawn as Japanese from 29 August 1910, the day the Treaty of Annexation was promulgated and took effect (Art. 8). It was signed on 22 August; CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, records the signing day and starts the colony on 23 August.
notes.jp: 1910 年 8 月 29 日——韓国併合条約が公布され施行された日（第 8 条）——から日本の統治下として描いている。調印は 8 月 22 日で、この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は調印日を記録し、植民地を 8 月 23 日から始めている。

notes.en: Under United States administration from 29 January 1946 (SCAPIN-677) until 15 May 1972; the Tokara Islands returned in 1952 and the Amami Islands in 1953. Japan kept residual sovereignty: the Treaty of San Francisco (Art. 3) placed the islands under US administration without transferring them. IntMap draws who governed the ground; CShapes 2.0, the source of these outlines, records sovereignty only and keeps them in Japan.
notes.jp: 1946 年 1 月 29 日（SCAPIN-677）から 1972 年 5 月 15 日まで米国の施政権下にあった（トカラ列島は 1952 年、奄美群島は 1953 年に復帰）。日本は潜在主権を保った——サンフランシスコ平和条約第 3 条は施政権を米国に置いただけで、領土を移していない。IntMap はその土地を誰が治めていたかを描く。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は主権だけを記録し、これらの島を日本に含めている。

notes.en: From 29 January 1946 to 15 May 1972 the Nansei Islands south of 30°N (south of 29°N from 1952, and only the Ryukyu and Daito Islands from 1953) were under United States administration and are drawn as a separate outline; Japan kept residual sovereignty over them (Treaty of San Francisco, Art. 3).
notes.jp: 1946 年 1 月 29 日から 1972 年 5 月 15 日まで、北緯 30 度以南の南西諸島（1952 年からは北緯 29 度以南、1953 年からは琉球諸島と大東諸島だけ）は米国の施政権下にあり、別の輪郭として描いている。日本はそれらの島に潜在主権を保った（サンフランシスコ平和条約第 3 条）。

notes.en: Taiwan is drawn here until 1 June 1895: the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed on 17 April and ratified on 8 May, but the island was handed over to Japan only on 2 June (its Qing officials had proclaimed the Republic of Formosa on 25 May). CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, records the signing day.
notes.jp: 台湾をここでは 1895 年 6 月 1 日までこの輪郭に含めて描いている。下関条約は 4 月 17 日に調印され 5 月 8 日に批准されたが、島が日本に引き渡されたのは 6 月 2 日である（清の官吏は 5 月 25 日に台湾民主国を宣言していた）。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は調印日を記録している。

notes.en: Drawn as Japanese from 2 June 1895, the day Taiwan was handed over under the Treaty of Shimonoseki. The treaty was signed on 17 April; CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, records the signing day and starts the colony then.
notes.jp: 1895 年 6 月 2 日——下関条約にもとづき台湾が引き渡された日——から日本の統治下として描いている。条約の調印は 4 月 17 日で、この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は調印日を記録し、その日から植民地を始めている。

notes.en: Drawn as a United States territory from 12 August 1898, the day sovereignty was transferred at ʻIolani Palace; the Republic of Hawaii governed until then. The Newlands Resolution was passed in July; CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, starts the territory on 6 July.
notes.jp: 1898 年 8 月 12 日——イオラニ宮殿で主権が移された日——から米国の領土として描いている。それまではハワイ共和国が統治していた。ニューランズ決議の成立は 7 月で、この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は 7 月 6 日から領土を始めている。

notes.en: Southern Ireland is drawn in the United Kingdom until 5 December 1922: the Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed on 6 December 1921, and the Irish Free State came into being on 6 December 1922 (from January 1922 the Provisional Government administered it inside the United Kingdom). CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, records the signing day.
notes.jp: 南アイルランドをここでは 1922 年 12 月 5 日まで英国に含めて描いている。英愛条約の調印は 1921 年 12 月 6 日で、アイルランド自由国が成立したのは 1922 年 12 月 6 日である（1922 年 1 月からは暫定政府が英国の中で行政を担った）。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は調印日を記録している。

notes.en: Drawn as a separate state from 6 December 1922, the day the Irish Free State came into being. The Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed on 6 December 1921; CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, records the signing day.
notes.jp: 1922 年 12 月 6 日——アイルランド自由国が成立した日——から別の国として描いている。英愛条約の調印は 1921 年 12 月 6 日で、この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は調印日を記録している。

notes.en: The Free City of Danzig is drawn until 31 August 1939: it was annexed to Germany on 1 September 1939, the day the Second World War began. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, ends it a year earlier (31 August 1938) and draws it inside Germany from 30 September 1938.
notes.jp: 自由都市ダンツィヒは 1939 年 8 月 31 日まで描いている。ドイツへの併合は、第二次世界大戦が始まった 1939 年 9 月 1 日である。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は 1 年早い 1938 年 8 月 31 日で終わらせ、1938 年 9 月 30 日からドイツの中に描いている。

notes.en: Bukovina is drawn in Austria from 3 to 10 November 1918: it was a crown land of the Austrian half of the monarchy, not of Hungary, where CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, places it. In those days Ukrainian and Romanian national councils held it between them; the Romanian army entered Czernowitz on 11 November.
notes.jp: 1918 年 11 月 3〜10 日のブコヴィナはオーストリアに描いている。ブコヴィナは二重帝国のオーストリア側の王領で、この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 が置くハンガリーの領土ではなかった。この間はウクライナ人とルーマニア人の民族評議会が分けて押さえ、11 月 11 日にルーマニア軍がチェルノフツィ（チェルニウツィ）に入った。

notes.en: Bukovina is drawn in Romania from 11 November 1918, when the Romanian army entered Czernowitz; the General Congress of Bukovina voted for union with Romania on 28 November. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, draws it in Hungary, which never held it, until Austria renounced it by the Treaty of Saint-Germain (10 September 1919).
notes.jp: ブコヴィナは、ルーマニア軍がチェルノフツィ（チェルニウツィ）に入った 1918 年 11 月 11 日からルーマニアに描いている（11 月 28 日にブコヴィナ総会がルーマニアとの合同を決議）。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は、オーストリアがサン＝ジェルマン条約（1919 年 9 月 10 日）で放棄するまで、一度も領有していないハンガリーの中に描いている。

notes.en: Southern Sakhalin is drawn up to the fiftieth parallel, the boundary the Treaty of Portsmouth (1905) set. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, ends it about 11 km further south and places the strip between in Russia.
notes.jp: 南樺太は、ポーツマス条約（1905 年）が定めた北緯 50 度線まで描いている。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は約 11 km 南で終わらせ、その間の帯をロシアに含めている。

notes.en: Germany is drawn with the Memel (Klaipėda) Territory north of the Neman until 14 February 1920 and with the Hlučín Region until 3 February 1920; both were Prussian, and the Treaty of Versailles detached them. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, carries today's borders back over them, placing the Memel Territory in Russia (then Lithuania) and the Hlučín Region in Austria-Hungary (then Czechoslovakia).
notes.jp: ドイツは、ネマン川以北のメーメル（クライペダ）地方を 1920 年 2 月 14 日まで、フルチーン地方を 1920 年 2 月 3 日まで含めて描いている。どちらもプロイセン領で、ヴェルサイユ条約で切り離された。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は今日の国境を遡らせ、メーメル地方をロシア（続いてリトアニア）に、フルチーン地方をオーストリア＝ハンガリー（続いてチェコスロバキア）に含めている。

notes.en: Germany is drawn with the Memel (Klaipėda) Territory until 14 February 1920, when a French administration took it over for the Allied Powers under the Treaty of Versailles. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, places it in Lithuania.
notes.jp: ドイツは、ヴェルサイユ条約に基づき連合国のためにフランスの行政府が引き継いだ 1920 年 2 月 15 日の前日まで、メーメル（クライペダ）地方を含めて描いている。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 はこの地方をリトアニアに含めている。

notes.en: The Memel (Klaipėda) Territory was governed by a High Commissioner of the Allied Powers from 15 February 1920 until Lithuania took it over on 19 February 1923, after the Klaipėda Revolt. CShapes 2.0, the source of these outlines, draws it in Lithuania throughout.
notes.jp: メーメル（クライペダ）地方は、1920 年 2 月 15 日から、クライペダ蜂起を経てリトアニアが引き継いだ 1923 年 2 月 19 日まで、連合国の高等弁務官が統治した。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は、この間もリトアニアに含めている。

notes.en: Germany is drawn with the Memel (Klaipėda) Territory from 23 March 1939, when Lithuania ceded it, until the Red Army took Memel on 28 January 1945. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, leaves it in Lithuania, then in the Soviet Union.
notes.jp: ドイツは、リトアニアがメーメル（クライペダ）地方を割譲した 1939 年 3 月 23 日から、赤軍がメーメルを占領した 1945 年 1 月 28 日の前日まで、この地方を含めて描いている。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は、リトアニア、続いてソ連に含めたままにしている。

notes.en: Italy is drawn with Istria, the Julian hinterland of Gorizia and Trieste, Zara and the islands of Cres and Lošinj from the Treaty of Rapallo (12 November 1920), and with Fiume from 22 February 1924, until the armistice of 8 September 1943; the line is OpenHistoricalMap's. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, carries Yugoslavia's post-war border back over this ground.
notes.jp: イタリアは、ラパッロ条約（1920 年 11 月 12 日）からイストリア、ゴリツィアとトリエステの後背地、ザラ（ザダル）、ツレス島・ロシニ島を、1924 年 2 月 22 日からはフィウメ（リエカ）も含めて、1943 年 9 月 8 日の休戦まで描いている。線は OpenHistoricalMap による。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は、戦後のユーゴスラビアの国境をこの土地に遡らせている。

notes.en: Hungary is drawn with Uzhhorod, Mukachevo and Berehove from the First Vienna Award (2 November 1938), and with the rest of Carpatho-Ukraine from its annexation on 16 March 1939, until the Soviet offensive of October 1944; the line is OpenHistoricalMap's. CShapes 2.0, the source of this outline, leaves this ground in Czechoslovakia.
notes.jp: ハンガリーは、第一次ウィーン裁定（1938 年 11 月 2 日）からウジホロド・ムカチェヴォ・ベレホヴェを、1939 年 3 月 16 日の併合からはカルパト・ウクライナの残りも含めて、1944 年 10 月のソ連軍の攻勢まで描いている。線は OpenHistoricalMap による。この輪郭の出典 CShapes 2.0 は、この土地をチェコスロバキアに残している。

examined.finding: Iturup, Kunashir, Shikotan and the Habomai islands (and Urup) have no polygon in CShapes 2.0 in any year, in Japan or in Russia/the Soviet Union.
examined.why: Nothing is claimed there, so nothing is wrong to correct: data/hist-borders-late.js (OpenHistoricalMap on CShapes' days) draws them in the Empire of Japan to 1923, and from 1924 the ground is drawn by no record. Filling it needs a source for the shape, not a move between two CShapes records.

examined.finding: The Bonin (Ogasawara) and Volcano Islands, the Daito Islands and the Tokara Islands have no polygon in CShapes 2.0. The Bonin and Volcano Islands were under United States administration from 29 January 1946 (SCAPIN-677) to 26 June 1968.
examined.why: No record draws these islands from 1886, so there is no polygon to move; the US administration of the Bonin Islands has nothing on the map to attach to.

examined.finding: CShapes starts Southern Sakhalin (7351) on 5 September 1905, the day the Treaty of Portsmouth was signed; ratifications were exchanged on 25 November 1905.
examined.why: Japan occupied Sakhalin in July 1905 and governed the southern half from then on, so on the signing day the ground was already Japan's to govern; the signing day is not later than the day of rule, unlike Korea, where the Korean Empire governed until the treaty took effect. The outline (the 50th parallel) is the treaty's.

examined.finding: CShapes draws Taiwan inside China from 15 August 1945 to 7 December 1949, although Japan renounced it only by the Treaty of San Francisco (in force 28 April 1952).
examined.why: The Republic of China took over the administration of Taiwan on 25 October 1945 and governed it from then on, so for 1945-1952 the record already draws who governed the ground — the convention IntMap applies to the Ryukyu Islands. The 71 days from 15 August to 24 October 1945 are CShapes' end-of-empire day, the same day it uses for Korea and Southern Sakhalin; no source states another single day on which the Japanese government's authority over Taiwan ceased before the hand-over.

examined.finding: CShapes draws the territorial clauses of the Treaty of Versailles on 28 June 1919, the signing day (France, Germany, Poland, Danzig, the Cameroons, Togoland, Tanganyika and others); the treaty took effect on 10 January 1920.
examined.why: No single day is right for all the ground one row boundary carries. Alsace-Lorraine was governed by France from the armistice of November 1918, most of Posen by the Polish insurgents from early 1919, and the German colonies by the occupying powers from 1914-1916 — all before the signing day — while West Prussia was handed to Poland only in January-February 1920 and Danzig passed from Germany to Allied administration on 10 January 1920 and became a Free City on 15 November 1920. Moving Germany's one boundary to 10 January 1920 would draw Alsace-Lorraine and Posen German for months they were not; the Danzig and West Prussia days need the rows split by region, which this ledger cannot express as one change of a code.

examined.finding: The preliminary surrender at Reims was signed on 7 May 1945 and took effect on 8 May.
examined.why: CShapes already draws the end of the German Reich and the occupation zones on 8 May 1945, the day the surrender took effect; the record is on the effective day.

examined.finding: The Polish-Soviet border agreement was signed on 16 August 1945 and took effect on 5 February 1946; the changes CShapes makes within three days are the end of the Japanese empire (15 August) and Indonesia (17 August).
examined.why: The agreement concerns neither of the changes it meets. Poland's eastern border is drawn by CShapes from 8 May 1945; the Soviet Union governed that ground from its reoccupation in 1944, so the agreement's later effective day is not the day the ground changed hands.

examined.finding: CShapes moves the Hungarian-Czechoslovak border on 10 February 1947 (the three villages of the Bratislava bridgehead, Rusovce, Jarovce and Čunovo) — the signing day of the Paris peace treaties. The item raised is the Treaty of Peace with Italy, signed the same day and in force on 15 September 1947.
examined.why: The treaty with Italy is not the instrument of this change: the villages were transferred by the Treaty of Peace with Hungary (Art. 1(4)), signed the same day and also in force on 15 September 1947. The day Czechoslovakia took over their administration is not established by any source read for this review, so the record is left on the signing day and the question stays open (dev-notes/2026-10-07-hist-findings-sweep.md).

examined.finding: CShapes moves Crimea from Ukraine to Russia on 18 March 2014, the day the treaty of accession was signed; Russia ratified it and it took effect on 1 April 2014 (Wikidata P7588).
examined.why: Russian forces had taken control of the peninsula from 27 February 2014, before the signing day, so the later effective day is not the day the ground changed hands. The annexation is not recognised (UN General Assembly resolution 68/262, 27 March 2014); the record draws who governed, which is the convention of this ledger.

examined.finding: Instruments signed within three days of a CShapes change, with a later effective date, that are about something else: bilateral investment treaties, Council of Europe conventions and protocols, environmental protocols (Kyoto, Volatile Organic Compounds), START II, and the Treaty of Osimo (Italy-Yugoslavia, 10 November 1975, met on the day of Angola's independence).
examined.why: None of them is the instrument of a change CShapes draws on the day it meets: an investment treaty, a convention or an arms-control treaty moves no border, and the Treaty of Osimo concerns two states CShapes does not change within three days of it. They are listed so that the finder's photograph is judged whole and a new candidate arrives counted.

examined.finding: CShapes draws Lviv, and all of Galicia, in «Austria» from 3 November 1918 to 9 September 1919.
examined.why: Galicia was a crown land of the Austrian half of the monarchy, and CShapes keeps all of that half (Galicia, Carniola, the Littoral, Dalmatia) under Austria until the Treaty of Saint-Germain, by whose Article 91 Austria renounced the former monarchy's lands outside its new frontiers — a sovereignty reading, not a statement of who governed. Who governed Galicia in those ten months was not one owner along one line: the Polish Liquidation Commission held West Galicia from the end of October 1918, while in East Galicia the West Ukrainian People's Republic and Poland fought along a moving front (Poland held Lviv from 22 November 1918 and took the rest of East Galicia by July 1919). No record IntMap carries draws those fronts, so a cut there would put a line on the map that no source states (dev-notes/2026-10-13-cshapes-review-cuts.md).

examined.finding: From 12 November 1920 to 21 February 1924 the city of Fiume (Rijeka) is drawn in Yugoslavia.
examined.why: The Treaty of Rapallo made Fiume a free state (Gabriele D'Annunzio's Regency of Carnaro held the city until the end of December 1920), and it was annexed to Italy on 22 February 1924 — from that day the cut julian-march-1924 draws it in Italy. Drawing the Free State of Fiume needs a unit of its own, as the Memel Territory has (3681); it is not one of the findings this review was opened for, and the cut julian-march-1920 leaves the city where CShapes puts it rather than in Italy, which did not hold it.

examined.finding: Istria and the Julian March are drawn in Austria from 3 November 1918 and in Yugoslavia from 10 September 1919 to 11 November 1920, and again in Yugoslavia from 9 September 1943.
examined.why: From November 1918 Italian troops held the ground up to the armistice line of the Treaty of London, which reached further than the Rapallo border (into Dalmatia, to Šibenik and Knin); no record IntMap carries draws that line, so the cut starts on the day the Treaty of Rapallo was signed, when Italy already held the ground it confirms. After the armistice of 8 September 1943 Germany occupied the region (the Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral), Yugoslav and Allied forces divided it in 1945 (the Morgan Line), and Italy's sovereignty ended only with the Treaty of Peace of 1947; none of those owners has a row on these days. Lastovo and Palagruža, Italian under Article 3 of the Treaty of Rapallo, have no polygon in CShapes, so nothing is drawn there to move.

examined.finding: CShapes keeps Bohemia, Moravia and Slovakia in Czechoslovakia from March 1939 to 1945 (the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia, the Slovak Republic, and the strip of eastern Slovakia Hungary took on 4 April 1939 are not drawn).
examined.why: This review cuts Subcarpathian Ruthenia out of Czechoslovakia for the years Hungary governed it, because Hungary is a record CShapes already draws there. The German protectorate and the Slovak state have no record at all; drawing them is a decision about the whole country for six years, not a correction of one region, and it is left to a review of its own. The 4 April 1939 strip (Sobrance and Stakčín) is measured at 1,067 km² in OpenHistoricalMap against about 1,700 km² in the literature, so its line is not settled enough to cut along.

examined.finding: The ground CShapes 2.0 adds to Romania on 10 September 1919 — the region the cuts bukovina-austria-1918 and bukovina-romania-1918 move — is 12,711 km², against 10,421 km² for OpenHistoricalMap's Duchy of Bukovina (1878-1918) and the duchy's stated 10,441 km²: about 2,650 km² of it lies outside the duchy (pieces of Maramureș in the west, of Galicia in the north, of Moldavia in the south and east), and about 360 km² of the duchy lies outside it.
examined.why: The cuts move exactly the ground CShapes itself hands to Romania on 10 September 1919, so Romania's outline does not change shape when CShapes' own row begins — the cut adds no new line, and the coarse line is CShapes' outline of Romania's Bukovina from 1919 to 1940. Redrawing that line is a correction of Romania's border for all those years, with OpenHistoricalMap's duchy as the line, and is left to a review of its own (dev-notes/2026-10-13-cshapes-review-cuts.md).

examined.finding: Southern Sakhalin (7351) covers 33,544 km² with the strip to the 50th parallel restored, against the 36,090 km² Karafuto Prefecture reported.
examined.why: The remaining difference is CShapes 2.0's generalised coastline (and Kaiba Island, which has no polygon), not a border: the outline now reaches the treaty's parallel. The coast is the subject of the coast records (data/hist-coast-snap.js), not of this ledger.
